title: Co-reading explainer gallery — audited interactive figures of what a language model writes when asked to reason about a geometric configuration
description:
A gallery of co-reading explainers: interactive isometric figures (also anywidgets for Jupyter / marimo), 1920×1080 stills, two-voice scripts and ledgers of what can and cannot be said, each built only from the frozen outputs of a pre-registered line of measurements whose cards (PREREG = the frozen promise written before the run, RESULT = the read-out written after it, corrections appended and never edited in) are included verbatim in Japanese with an English index. Every number on a page is anchored to the data by a checker with a positive control (check_claims.py); the question texts are traced to the public ConstructGap suite (v1.0.1) with an md5 at every stage; each figure was judged under seal by readers from a different model family than its maker.

The gallery is read as one line of three stations: moy-2 (from algebraic analysis to elementary geometry — a reflection formula offered to OLMo-3 32B base as a tool; what it computes and what it writes in its proof field), moy-1 (elementary geometry) and moy-5 (how to make a model draw the auxiliary line). This release contains station 1.

View the figures on GitHub Pages: https://moyhig-ecs.github.io/coread-explainer-gallery/ (the hash in a page URL is the state; #s19 is the ledger). Run them from this archive: unzip, open <entry>/dist/<page>.html (the pages are self-contained) or serve the folder with python3 -m http.server. Zenodo does not render HTML.

Made with the coread-explainer skill for Claude Code on the Anatomy kit (MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 Ryan). Gallery: MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 Manabu Higashida; the quoted model outputs are data.
